summary.headline: Chola Q4 FY26 disbursements rose 25% YoY to INR32,913 crore, AUM up 21% to INR2,42,630 crore; FY27 credit cost guided to ~1.5% pre-overlay.
summary.overview: Disbursements grew 25% YoY in Q4 across all major product segments, with Vehicle Finance up 26% and Consumer up 45%. NIM rose 40 bps YoY to about 8% on lower cost of funds, and pre-overlay ROA was 4.1% versus 3.6% a year earlier. Management booked a INR200 crore precautionary management overlay for geopolitical and fuel-price risks, and said April 2026 early delinquencies, non-starters and first-cut net credit losses were better than April 2025. Guidance for FY27 is 20-23% AUM growth and net credit cost falling from 1.6% (pre-overlay) to about 1.5%.

segments.name: Vehicle Finance
segments.commentary: Disbursements grew 26% YoY in Q4 and AUM 18% to INR1,19,558 crore. FY27 guidance is disbursement growth of 15-20% and AUM growth of about 18%; April showed growth across PV, 2W, HCV and LCV.

segments.name: MSME (LAP, SME, SBPL)
segments.commentary: MSME disbursements grew 11% in Q4 and AUM 29%. LAP AUM INR52,295 crore (+26%), SME INR9,338 crore (+41%), SBPL INR3,537 crore (+46%).

segments.name: Consumer (Home Loans, CSEL, Gold, CD)
segments.commentary: Consumer disbursements grew 45% YoY, with gold loan disbursing INR1,130 crore in Q4 and Consumer AUM up 20%; Home Loan AUM +23%, and CSEL AUM +4%. Home loan disbursements moderated due to election-related and land-record delays.

segments.name: CSEL
segments.commentary: Loan losses fell to 5.2% in Q4 and Q4 ROA was 2.3%. Management targets pre-tax ROA above 3% this year and CSEL portfolio growth of about 20% by Q4 FY27 from about 4% currently; Q4 opex included a one-time CGTMSE cost.

guidance_outlook: FY27 overall AUM growth of 20-23%; LAP and Home Loans 25-30%, Vehicle Finance about 18%, SME/SBPL above 30%.
Net credit cost to fall from 1.6% pre-overlay to about 1.5% in FY27; management frames 1.4% as a possible FY28 level.
NIM to hold at about 8%; opex to stay around 3.0-3.1% of average assets, with no operating leverage assumed for about a year.
Pre-tax ROTA target of about 3.5%; CSEL pre-tax ROA to exceed 3%.
Gold loan to add about 360 branches (119 today) and Home Loans about 100 branches in FY27; gold branches exclusive, others co-located.
capex_capacity: Home Loan branches: about 60 in Q1 and 40 in Q2 FY27, taking Home Loan branches to about 100 added in the year.
Gold loan: about 360 new exclusive branches, taking the count from 119 to about 480.
Collections headcount is about 30,000; CSEL, consumer durables and CD are also to add about 100 branches each.
Capital: management would evaluate equity if Tier 1 approaches 13%; otherwise internal accruals expected to suffice for growth below 23-25%.
Remaining CCD balance of INR630 crore expected to convert in H1 FY27.
demand_pricing: Management reported strong April 2026 sales, credit and collections versus April 2025, and no change in customer behaviour at the ground level.
Balraj Menon said April early defaults and non-starters were significantly lower than April 2025 and in line with prior-year April-March trends; first-cut net credit losses were also lower.
Gold loan average ticket size has fallen from about INR3 lakh to about INR2 lakh, with per-customer exposure of INR5-6 lakh; yield cited at about 15%.
Competition from banks in vehicle finance has not changed significantly over the past four to five months, including in April.
Home loan disbursements of INR1,800-2,000 crore a quarter have been flat for about seven or eight quarters; FY27 home loan disbursement growth guided at 12-15%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 AUM and credit cost trajectory, and what credit filter changes are being made?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth stays at 20-23% and net credit cost is expected to fall from 1.6% pre-overlay to about 1.5%, helped by Gini-coefficient improvements in underwriting. No further overlay is needed for now beyond the INR200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the strong April CV and PV data from OEMs reflected on the ground?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said April sales, credit and collections were very strong versus April 2025, and it has seen no change in customer behaviour.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CSEL growth, opex and ROA outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CSEL pre-tax ROA is expected to exceed 3% this year from Q4 ROA of 2.3%. Q4 opex included a one-time CGTMSE cost (about 6% of the segment's opex), and the opex ratio should normalise to about 4.5%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the business loan book is covered by CGTMSE?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70% of unsecured assets are covered and this may rise to 80-82%. Only the business loan book is in CGTMSE, at about INR3,000-3,500 crore (about 80% of a roughly INR5,000 crore BL book); Q4 CGTMSE cost was about INR38 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Did the overlay change PD-LGD assumptions, and why is NIM up 50 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: No PD-LGD change was made; the overlay was set using COVID and diesel-price experience. The NIM jump relates to ARC receipts recognised as income, offset by higher credit losses, leaving ROTA largely unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital-raising policy and gearing guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity raising would be evaluated if Tier 1 approaches 13%. Growth below 23-25% is expected to be funded from internal accruals. Gearing fell from 7.17x to 6.94x.

risks_watch: Geopolitical and fuel-price pressure on HCV long-haul operators; management says HCVs are only 5-7% of Vehicle Finance AUM.
Gold loan build-out (about 360 branches) adds cost and needs experienced staff; operating leverage deferred about a year.
Home loan disbursements stuck around INR1,800-2,000 crore a quarter; the southern-state election delays may persist.
Fintech run-down book of INR300-400 crore has a long tail through the year.
Cost of funds may rise marginally in FY27, offsetting newer-business yield gains.
Rating upgrade from AA+ is under discussion with agencies; ICRA has a positive outlook.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on asset quality and April trends, and on Vehicle Finance recovery and market-share gains. Cautious on the global outlook, which led to the INR200 crore overlay. Evasive on the gold-loan breakeven and on business-wise disbursement splits, which were withheld.
key_quotes: As of now, at the ground level, we have not observed any change in customer behavior.
We are also expecting our net credit cost to decline from 1.6% pre-overlay to around 1.5%.
Historically, this has been in the range of 1% to 1.2% but redefining a steady -state level will take time.
There is no fixed formula whereby achieving certain metrics automatically results in an upgrade.
